description: Single source of the rasterizer perf-regression gate. scripts/check-raster-perf-baseline.sh reads a measured BenchmarkDotNet run (its full JSON export) and works with each benchmark's speed index, r = measured / baselineMs. Two checks: (1) relative — each benchmark's r divided by the geometric mean of r over the OTHER benchmarks marked 'reference' must not exceed 1 + relativeTolerance, so a regression confined to one code path fails however fast or slow the runner is; (2) suite — the geometric mean of r over every 'reference' benchmark must not exceed 1 + suiteTolerance, a backstop for a slowdown that hits everything at once. Independently of any measurement, the script runs the SSIM-LOOSEN-shaped governance check: raising a baselineMs, relativeTolerance or suiteTolerance, or taking a benchmark out of the reference set, needs a 'PERF-LOOSEN:' commit-message token; tightening always passes.
runner: linux-x64, GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest (4 logical cores since 2026-09-30; the gate prints the runner's CPU and core count), net8.0, BenchmarkDotNet --job short (ci.yml's raster-perf-gate). Hosted runners land on several CPU models whose speed differs by up to ~2x, and any single run can be ~1.5x slower than usual on every benchmark at once (a busy host). The relative check cancels both; only the suite backstop sees raw speed, which is why it is the loose one.
calibrationNote: baselineMs is the median of the per-commit gate's own readings over 59 distinct raster-perf-gate jobs from 2026-10-05 to 2026-10-22 (AMD EPYC 7763 x30, 9V45 x15, 9V74 x9, Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C x3, Xeon 6973P-C x2; a re-run attempt that repeats an earlier job's log counts once), not a full-job calibration mean, so r is centred on what the gate itself measures. Each relativeTolerance covers the largest relative ratio seen with about 10% to spare, rounded up to 0.05 with a floor of 0.25; the single-threaded bands also cover 41 earlier jobs (2026-09-28/29, same code, 2-core runners), except that ImageHeavyPage's 0.5 clears its one 1.47 spike by only 2% rather than widening to 0.65 (see its description). suiteTolerance is sized the same way from the slowest job's suite speed (1.51), a run the previous raw-time gate failed on runner noise alone. Replayed through this script, none of the 59 jobs fails, and of the 41 earlier ones only FourDocumentsInParallel fails (2-core runners). In a typical job a regression in one benchmark fails from about 1.28x (Jpx, Minify), 1.33x (Magnify), 1.46x (Image), 1.52x (Text), 1.72x (FourDocumentsInParallel) or 2.2x (Transparency); one that hits everything at once fails only past the suite backstop (1.7x the baselines' speed), so on the fastest runners (9V45, ~0.6x) a uniform slowdown can pass up to ~2.8x. To re-derive after a deliberate performance change: scripts/harvest-raster-perf-readings.sh prints the medians and worst ratios from recent CI jobs. A benchmark made faster should have its baselineMs lowered in the same change (free under governance): leaving it high lowers the reference the others are compared with.

RasterizeBenchmarks.RasterizeTextHeavyPa.description: 55 short paragraphs (~9pt) on one A4 page at 2048px width — glyph-shaping and glyph-rasterization throughput. Its relative ratio ran up to 1.42 (one Intel model runs text comparatively slowly), hence the wider band.

RasterizeBenchmarks.RasterizeImageHeavyP.description: Six distinct 300x200 gradient images stacked on one A4 page at 2048px width — image-XObject decode/blit throughput. Relative ratio ran up to 1.22, plus one 1.47 spike (this benchmark alone, in an otherwise normal run), hence 0.5 rather than 0.35.

RasterizeBenchmarks.RasterizeTransparenc.description: A rotated watermark plus four partially-transparent corner stamps over body content, one A4 page at 2048px width — alpha-compositing throughput. At ~11 ms with a bimodal distribution its relative ratio ran up to 2.02, so it has the widest band and is kept out of the reference set the others are compared with.

RasterizeBenchmarks.RasterizeFourDocumen.description: Four independent PdfDocument.Open + Rasterize calls (each its own scratch ObjectRegistry) racing via Parallel.For — wall-clock throughput. Core count and neighbour load move it differently from single-threaded work (relative ratio up to 1.54), so it is compared with the reference set but not part of it. Concurrency correctness is proven separately by the raster-concurrency-stress pixel-identity lane. Its band assumes 4-logical-core runners: on the 2-core runners CI used until 2026-09-29 it reads about 2x and fails.

RasterizeBenchmarks.RasterizeJpxScanPage.description: A self-contained one-page PDF (composed byte-wise in [GlobalSetup], no corpus dependency) placing a 640x480 JPEG 2000 scan (9/7 irreversible, ICT, tiled RPCL) full-page — JPX decode-and-paint throughput. Relative ratio ran up to 1.07.

RasterizeBenchmarks.RasterizeScanPageMin.description: A self-contained one-page scan-shaped placement rendered through the minify (box-filter) regime — the resampling knob's minify path. Relative ratio ran up to 1.13.

RasterizeBenchmarks.RasterizeScanPageMag.description: The same scan-shaped placement rendered through the magnify (bilinear/nearest) regime — the resampling knob's magnify path. Relative ratio ran up to 1.15.
